newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India cancels second gasoline import tender-trader.
newsitem.headline: India cancels second gasoline import tender-trader.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has cancelled its second gasoline purchase tender in a row, traders said on Friday.
IOC has cancelled its tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of 87-octane, 0.15 grams per litre leaded gasoline for September 23-27 delivery to Kandla on the Indian west coast.
The tender had closed on August 13 and was scheduled for a one-day validity.
At the end of July, IOC cancelled a previous tender for a cargo for August 10-14 delivery, as IOC had over-estimated its demand, an Indian source said.
The source had said that while there was "no reason for the cancellation" of the August tender, there were no refinery shutdowns to spur the issue of the September tender either.
IOC last purchased gasoline by tender in June due to a shortfall caused by the five-day emergency shutdown of the 150,000-barrel-per-day Cochin refinery in early June.

It bought a 25,000-tonne gasoline cargo for June 18-22 delivery at $43 per tonne above Mideast naphtha quotes and another at more than $30 per tonne premium for June 26-30 delivery. Both cargoes were delivered on a cost-and-freight basis to Bombay on the west coast, traders said.
